# Jepson Center & Telfair Children's Art Museum

Hours

Open 10am–5pm today

[View Hours](https://www.telfair.org/visit/jepson-center/# 'Regular Hours')

The Jepson Center links the history preserved by the Owens-Thomas House & Slave Quarters and Telfair Academy to the future of art and architecture. The strikingly modern building, opened in 2006, is filled with art, activities, and educational opportunities that will encourage learning for generations to come.

Address [207 W. ## Jepson Center: History and Harmony

After a century of collecting, exhibiting, and educating Savannah and its visitors about art, history, and architecture, Telfair Museums’ Director and Board of Trustees identified the need for a new, larger facility. Their primary objectives were to increase the capacity for traveling exhibitions, continue an emphasis on education and community involvement, and increase archival storage for a growing collection. The museums’ Board of Directors envisioned a building representative of its time but also open, welcoming, and inviting. They also understood that, in a National Historic Landmark District, it would be challenging to express these ideals in architecture.

Five internationally recognized architectural firms presented their ideas to the trustees in 1998. The trustees unanimously chose Moshe Safdie and Associates. Safdie offered an outstanding international track record of responsible, compelling designs in historic settings, and he excited them with his passion about the possibilities of the new project. Safdie also offered a clear and stimulating vision of a building that would harmonize with its surroundings and welcome the community.

What nobody envisioned was a two-year controversy surrounding the proposed project as the design team made its case before Savannah’s Historic Review Board. Only the passion and dedication of countless individuals enabled the grand vision for the Jepson Center to endure, providing Savannah with a truly iconic structure that, in the words of Safdie, is “vital, contemporary, appropriate to the expression of art to come … and a building you cannot conceive of anywhere else but Savannah.”

**Now On View**[**Michelangelo’s Women: Images of Female Power and Divinity from the Casa Buonarroti**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/michelangelos-women-images-of-female-power-and-divinity-from-the-casa-buonarroti/)October 9, 2026 – to January 24, 2027 Jepson Center

Drawn from the historic collections of the artist’s own family, Michelangelo’s Women uses his drawings, poetry, and letters, some never before seen in the United States, to encourage visitors to think about the ways that Michelangelo looked at women and what women saw in his works.

## Exhibitions

[**#art912, A Seat at the Table**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/art912-a-seat-at-the-table/)January 9 – to December 6, 2026 Jepson Center

_A Seat at the Table_ is a solo exhibition of figurative paintings on canvas and a site-specific mural by artist Julia Roland (b. 2002). A recent graduate of SCAD who grew up in Savannah, Roland’s identity as a queer Black woman from the American South informs her practice, but she sees the works speaking broadly to the human need for community.

Learn More

[**Michelangelo’s Women: Images of Female Power and Divinity from the Casa Buonarroti**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/michelangelos-women-images-of-female-power-and-divinity-from-the-casa-buonarroti/)October 9, 2026 – to January 24, 2027 Jepson Center

Drawn from the historic collections of the artist’s own family, Michelangelo’s Women uses his drawings, poetry, and letters, some never before seen in the United States, to encourage visitors to think about the ways that Michelangelo looked at women and what women saw in his works.

Learn More

[**Remember the Ladies: Women Who Made Telfair**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/remember-the-ladies-women-who-made-telfair/)October 9, 2026 – to January 24, 2027 Jepson Center

Remember the Ladies honors just a few of the many significant women who have impacted Telfair Museums with a new examination of their important contributions. It features highlights written by women curators to inspire the next generation to continue Mary Telfair’s legacy for years to come.

Learn More

[**Divided Loyalties: Stories of the American Revolution**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/divided-loyalties-stories-of-the-american-revolution/)July 24, 2026 – to February 28, 2027 Jepson Center

As the United States marks the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, Telfair Museums will feature works from the permanent collection that reveal the complications of living in revolutionary times, especially in Savannah. Portraits from the 18th century put faces to the challenges of this period. While colonial politicians and businessmen were at odds with families, friends, and partners, women made difficult decisions to protect themselves. Meanwhile, people of African and Indigenous descent were left out of critical conversations yet pulled into violent clashes.

Learn More

### Telfair Children’s Art Museum – _The World of William O. Golding_

Telfair celebrates a new exhibition in its immersive Children’s Art Museum that focuses on the fantastic art of Savannah artist and sailor William O. Golding (1874-1943). A host of new interactive experiences will lead children and adults through the remarkable story of this artist whose seafaring adventures of 49 years inspired his distinctive maritime drawings. New exhibits by FREN Inc. bring Golding’s pencil and crayon drawings to life in animations that visitors of all ages may control and interact with.

## #art912

#art912 is an initiative dedicated to raising the visibility and promoting the vitality of artists living and working in Savannah through exhibition opportunities, public programs, and outreach.

### Exhibition Opportunities

**Boxed In/Break Out** Artists are invited to submit proposals for a public art installation in the windows of the Jepson Center that face Barnard Street.

#### #art912 on Social Media

Telfair Museums encourages anyone who is making art, looking at art, or talking about art in Savannah to use [#art912](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/art912/?hl=en) on any social media platform to talk about art or artists in Savannah.

Answers to the most common questions about visiting the Getty Villa.

[See all FAQs](https://www.getty.edu/visit/villa/faqs)

- ### Is it free to visit?

 Admission is free, and requires a timed-entry reservation.

 Please note there is a fee for parking.

- ### How do I make reservations?

 [Make a free reservation online](https://tickets.getty.edu/Online/default.asp) or call [(310) 440-7300](tel:3104407300).

- ### How much does parking cost?

 Parking is $25 per car or motorcycle; $15 after 3pm. For evening events, parking is $10 after 6pm.

 Please note: Getty parking fees are cashless. All major banking/credit cards are accepted.

 (Rates include Los Angeles City Parking Occupancy Tax.)

- ### Are there Visitor Code of Conduct guidelines?

 Yes, we have a Visitor Code of Conduct.

 Getty is committed to fostering a safe, respectful, and welcoming environment for all. Our dedicated team works hard to ensure your visit is enjoyable and meaningful, and we are steadfast in supporting them in that mission.

 Our Expectations

 Please treat others with respect and kindness. Any behavior or language that is disrespectful, abusive, harassing, or threatening—including sexual harassment, unwelcome advances, or racial and other derogatory slurs—is strictly prohibited. Getty may refuse or revoke admission to individuals who violate this Code of Conduct and any other site rules, whether on print materials or as directed by Getty staff.

 A Shared Commitment

 Thank you for visiting Getty and contributing to a community built on mutual respect and understanding, where everyone feels they belong.

# Telfair Academy

Hours

Open 10am–5pm today

[View Hours](https://www.telfair.org/visit/telfair-academy/# 'Regular Hours')

The Telfair Academy is just a short walk away from the Jepson Center, but that short distance covers nearly 200 years of history. The stately two-story mansion was designed by British architect William Jay (1792–1837) in the neoclassical style and completed around 1820. It is just three historic squares away from Jay’s other masterpiece, the Owens-Thomas House & Slave Quarters. Transformed to a public art museum in 1886, the Telfair Academy contains 19th and 20th century American and European art from the museum’s permanent collection including paintings, works on paper, sculpture, and decorative arts.

Address [121 Barnard St. Savannah, GA 31401(external link)](https://goo.gl/maps/freQ1EL2yJE2)

Proximity

- [Jepson Center:](https://www.telfair.org/visit/jepson-center/) **1 min**
- [Owens-Thomas House & Slave Quarters:](https://www.telfair.org/visit/owens-thomas/) **7 mins**

[History](https://www.telfair.org/visit/telfair-academy/#history) [Exhibitions](https://www.telfair.org/visit/telfair-academy/#exhibitions) [Galleries](https://www.telfair.org/visit/telfair-academy/#galleries) [Bird Girl](https://www.telfair.org/visit/telfair-academy/#birdgirl)

## Telfair Academy: Art, History, and Architecture in Savannah

Designed for Alexander Telfair (1789–1832), the Telfair mansion was constructed around 1820 on the site of the former colonial Governor’s mansion. Alexander commissioned William Jay (1792–1837), a young English architect, to design his new home. Jay had recently arrived in Savannah from England to oversee the construction of the residence of Richard Richardson (1735–1833), now Telfair Museums’ [Owens–Thomas House & Slave Quarters](http://telfair.org/visit/owens-thomas/).

In 1875, Mary Telfair (1791–1875) – heir to the family fortune and last to bear the Telfair name – bequeathed the family home to the Georgia Historical Society upon her death to be opened as a public art museum. The Society hired German-born artist Carl Brandt (1831–1905) to create the new institution. Working with New York-based architect Detlef Lienau (1818–1887) and Savannah-based architect Carl Augustus Schwaab (1823-1899), Brandt remodeled the old Telfair home and constructed an addition to house a new collection of art. The museum opened to the public in 1886, making it the oldest public art museum in the South and the first museum in the United States founded by a woman.

In 1906, following the death of Brandt, Telfair Museums’ Board of Trustees asked American artist Gari Melchers (1860–1932) to serve as the museum’s fine arts advisor and to make purchases on its behalf. Melchers accepted, and during his tenure from 1906 to 1916, he facilitated the purchase of many of the best-known works in the permanent collection thanks to his many connections to the international art world.

Today, Mary Telfair’s unique gift to the city of Savannah has grown into an institution comprising three architecturally significant buildings, over 6,300 works of art, and a proud history of educational programming and exciting exhibitions.

## Exhibitions

[**Craft along the Coast**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/craft-along-the-coast/)March 28, 2025 - Ongoing Telfair Academy

The new _Craft along the Coast_ galleries feature works from Telfair's permanent collection that date from the 18th to the late 20th centuries. Gallery 1 presents examples of woodworking, ceramics, and painting, while Gallery 2 focuses on Savannah's silversmithing traditions. Both galleries tell stories of markets and craft legacies, helping to draw lines of continuity through a dynamic history.

Learn More

[**Roots in the Rushes: ** African American Basketry of the Lowcountry](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/roots-in-the-rushes-african-american-basketry-of-the-lowcountry/)April 24, 2026 – to April 4, 2027 Telfair Academy

_Roots in the Rushes: African American Basketry of the Lowcountry_ explores the intricate history of this basketmaking tradition in the region. These handsewn forms were largely found in Savannah and the greater coastal Georgia and South Carolina region and highlight the historical and cultural contributions of one of the Lowcountry’s oldest handicrafts of African origin.

Learn More

[**The Walter and Linda Evans Gallery of African American Art**](https://www.telfair.org/exhibitions/the-walter-and-linda-evans-gallery-of-african-american-art/)Ongoing Telfair Academy

In 2023, Dr. Walter and Linda Evans donated a transformational gift of 28 significant works by African American artists to Telfair Museums. The museum is proud to organize an exciting new installation in the former dining room at the Telfair Academy that centers on this collection.

Learn More

Photo by Adam Kuehl

## Originally placed in Bonaventure Cemetery, the Bird Girl was moved to Telfair Museums for safekeeping.

## You can now see her Tuesday through Sunday from 10am-5pm inside the Telfair Academy.

# Galleries

The original Telfair mansion was completed around 1820. On the exterior, architect William Jay’s (1792–1837) inspiration from ancient Greek and Roman architecture for design is reflected by the symmetrical façade and columns with cast stone capitals. On the interior, what were formerly living spaces including a reception room, dining room, drawing room, and bedrooms, as well as the annex addition that includes the spacious Rotunda and Sculpture Galleries, have been transformed to art galleries that feature exhibitions drawn from Telfair’s permanent collection. These galleries feature 18th and 19th century American and European fine and decorative art including paintings, sculpture, silver, and works on paper.

### Rotunda Gallery

Photo by Adam Kuehl

The Rotunda Gallery reflects the vision and taste of three important figures in the museum’s early history: Telfair’s first director, Carl Brandt (1831–1905); the architect of the space, German-born Detlef Lienau (1818–1887); and Gari Melchers (1860–1932), the museum’s fine arts advisor from 1906–1916. The Rotunda Gallery and the Sculpture Gallery are the result of an 1883–86 renovation that transformed the Telfair mansion into an art museum. Brandt worked with Lienau to design the Rotunda, which evokes the grandeur of a 19th-century European salon. Brandt also created the four murals on view in the upper register of the gallery. These depict the great practitioners of the four primary art forms according to Brandt: Apelles, painting (west); Iktinus, architecture (north); Praxiteles, sculpture (east); and Albrecht Dürer, printmaking (south). The fact that three of these artists are ancient Greeks reflects the late 19th-century reverence for classical art and culture.

### Sculpture Gallery

Photo by Adam Kuehl 

Part of the 1883–86 addition to the Telfair mansion, the Sculpture Gallery features classical architectural elements including four Ionic columns and clerestory windows punctuated by pilasters. Originally, a skylight placed in the center of the gallery’s ceiling transmitted light from the Rotunda above. The initial decoration of the Sculpture Gallery featured murals created by Carl Brandt of important archaeological sites that were installed in the panels between the windows.

The museum’s collection of plaster casts, which lend the Sculpture Gallery its name, are copies of famous Greco-Roman sculptures. Brandt originally ordered over 70 of these casts from major museums in Europe. Presented on the same scale as the original works, the casts were important to early Telfair Academy art students who sketched them as a critical step toward mastering life drawing. More importantly, the casts allowed the people of 19th century Savannah to appreciate the great works of Greco-Roman civilization without ever leaving home.

Today, the Sculpture Gallery primarily displays works from Telfair’s permanent collection, many of which were purchased by Gari Melchers. Highlights typically on view in this gallery include Childe Hassam’s _Brooklyn Bridge in Winter_, Frederick Carl Frieseke’s _The Hammock_, George Bellows’ _Snow-Capped River_, and Robert Henri’s _La Madrileñita_. These works illustrate the primary strengths of Telfair’s permanent collection in American impressionism and Ashcan School works.

### Upper Level Galleries

Originally, the upstairs served as private rooms for the Telfair family, likely bedrooms. In the 1880s, these spaces were modified into art galleries. The original windows and fireplaces were covered by walls suitable for hanging paintings. Today, these galleries display work from Telfair’s permanent collection and temporary exhibitions.

### Entrance Hall

Photo by Calvin Parker

The museum’s entrance hall bears little resemblance to the hall of the original Telfair house. A guest visiting the Telfairs would have entered through a small vestibule with an illusory domed ceiling and doors leading to the Octagon Room on the left and the double parlor on the right. Continuing into the hall, the visitor would have seen a double staircase, a landing, and a single stair leading to the upper level.

In the 1880s, the entrance hall was opened up to allow public groups to more easily enter what was once a private home. The original staircase was removed, as was the original octagonal skylight. Pine floors were covered in marble, and a marble staircase was installed at the end of the entrance hall leading to the upstairs bedrooms (also altered) and the new addition. The upper part of the entrance hall was originally open in the center with walkways on either side leading into the Telfairs’ bedrooms.

### _One Museum, Many Façades_

Photo by David Kaminsky

_One Museum, Many Façades_ presents the history of Telfair Museums in correlation with the development of its buildings, to offer visitors an entry point to the institution. “A Substantial Mansion” tells the story of the Telfair family and the construction of their home on St. James Square. “A Public Edifice” narrates the establishment of the Telfair Academy of Arts & Sciences in Mary Telfair’s will and key figures in the years that followed. “A Memorial” explains Margaret Gray Thomas’s connection to Telfair, her bequest of her family home to Telfair Museums, and the changes prompted by the rediscovery of the slave quarters in the 1990s. “A Dynamic Building” brings this history into the 21st century and asks visitors to consider the museum’s path forward.

## Featured FAQs

Answers to frequently asked questions about visiting the Getty Center

[See all FAQs](https://www.getty.edu/visit/center/faqs)

- ### Is it free to visit?

 Admission is free, and requires a timed-entry reservation.

 Please note there is a fee for parking.

- ### How do I make reservations?

 [Make a free reservation online](https://tickets.getty.edu/Online/default.asp) or call [(310) 440-7300](tel:3104407300).

- ### How much does parking cost?

 Parking is $25 per car or motorcycle; $15 after 3pm; $10 after 6pm.

 Saturdays after 6pm, parking is free.

 Please note: Getty parking fees have gone cashless. All major banking/credit cards are accepted.

 (Rates include Los Angeles City Parking Occupancy Tax.)

- ### Are there Visitor Code of Conduct guidelines?

 Yes, we have a Visitor Code of Conduct.

 Getty is committed to fostering a safe, respectful, and welcoming environment for all. Our dedicated team works hard to ensure your visit is enjoyable and meaningful, and we are steadfast in supporting them in that mission.

 Our Expectations

 Please treat others with respect and kindness. Any behavior or language that is disrespectful, abusive, harassing, or threatening—including sexual harassment, unwelcome advances, or racial and other derogatory slurs—is strictly prohibited. Getty may refuse or revoke admission to individuals who violate this Code of Conduct and any other site rules, whether on print materials or as directed by Getty staff.

 A Shared Commitment

 Thank you for visiting Getty and contributing to a community built on mutual respect and understanding, where everyone feels they belong.

- ### Why are some of the galleries closed?

 Getty is undergoing major modernization efforts that serve as an investment in overall visitor experience and will enhance accessibility, strengthen energy resilience, and support the long-term stewardship of the site’s iconic architecture. [Learn about Getty Center improvements.](https://www.getty.edu/about/building-gettys-future/)

Connecting people to art and creative practice.

KMAC is Louisville's premier educational contemporary art museum in historic downtown on Museum Row.

​

Through exhibitions, education, and outreach, KMAC works to fulfill our mission of connecting people to art and creative practice.

​

KMAC is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. Your contribution helps us sustain local creativity!

KMAC celebrates diversity and is committed to intentional, on-going work that fosters equity and facilitates accessibility. KMAC is deeply committed to providing art experiences for everyone. KMAC exists to spark curiosity, inspire meaningful connections, and foster a deep sense of inclusion, belonging, and purpose that ripples beyond the museum’s walls.

Members: Free 
Students with ID: Free

## Exhibitions [Show All](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibitions/current/)

### [Artists & Sense of Place Residency Pearl Divers: In the Waves](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/artists-sense-of-place-residency-6/)

///  November 9, 2026 - January 24, 2027

Teaching artist Jenny Fine worked with 160 elementary students from Young Audiences Charter School in the exploration of the world of microbes. Using Fine’s photographs as a starting point, students explored texture and the patterns of oyster shells before bringing their own oysters to life through sculpture.

[Read More](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/artists-sense-of-place-residency-6/)

### [The Dream is the Truth](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/the-dream-is-the-truth/)

///  July 25, 2026 - January 10, 2027

_The Dream is the Truth_ showcases a unique survey of artists whose practices fall within and across the categories of Vernacular Art, which broadly includes self-taught and Visionary Art, all drawn from Ogden Museum Collection. The exhibition features paintings, drawings and bricolage sculptures created within a grassroots Southern tradition of artmaking beyond academic or conventional art institutions. These artists deeply engage recurring themes of spirituality, memory, sense of place and community, often transforming found or repurposed materials through strikingly original expression and a strong sense of artistic purpose.

[Read More](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/the-dream-is-the-truth/)

### [In the Eyes and Mind of the Feral Child The Art of Tom McNease](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/in-the-eyes-and-mind-of-the-feral-child/)

///  September 12, 2026 - March 14, 2027

Tom McNease is a true enigma of Southern Art. Known as an eccentric recluse, McNease avoided the social trappings of the art world choosing instead to live an isolated existence among the swamps, bayous and rivers of Southeast Louisiana. The full depth and importance of McNease’s art practice was not known until after his death in 2014. This exhibition shines a light on this misunderstood and underappreciated artist whose contribution and innovative use of photography and painting has been overlooked due in part by his refusal to participate in the commercial art gallery and museum system.

[Read More](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/in-the-eyes-and-mind-of-the-feral-child/)

### [Louisiana Contemporary 2026 presented by The Helis Foundation](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/louisiana-contemporary-2026/)

///  August 1, 2026 - February 14, 2027

Ogden Museum of Southern Art first launched _Louisiana Contemporary_, presented by The Helis Foundation in 2012, as an annual survey exhibition that would bring to the fore the work of artists living in Louisiana and highlight the dynamism of art practice throughout the state. Since the inaugural exhibition, Ogden Museum has shown works by over 650 artists, making Louisiana Contemporary an important moment in the national arts calendar to recognize and experience the spectrum and vitality of artistic voices emanating from New Orleans and art communities across Louisiana.

[Read More](https://ogdenmuseum.org/exhibition/louisiana-contemporary-2026/)

#### Welcome to the GCMA

Considered one of the premier American art museums in the South, the Greenville County Museum of Art is home to the world’s largest public collection of watercolors by iconic American artist Andrew Wyeth, along with an exceptional collection of paintings and prints by contemporary artist Jasper Johns. Ranging from Federal portraits to contemporary abstractions, the Museum’s acclaimed Southern Collection offers visitors a rich survey of American art through works with deep connections to the South.

**\*Please note that works from the Wyeth and Johns collections are not always on view. Visitors are encouraged to check the Museum’s current [exhibitions page](https://gcma.org/see/) or call ahead for availability.**

The GCMA is also the only museum in the Upstate fully accredited by the American Alliance of Museums.

[Learn more](https://gcma.org/see/) [Plan your visit](https://gcma.org/visit/)

# This is the Everson 
**A Museum** 
**of Firsts.**

## **Tickets Now Available!**

Taking place from **December 3-12, 2026**, this beloved Central New York tradition brings together families and community members to celebrate the season with festive, hands-on activities, live music, performances, and, of course, the opportunity to enjoy the incredible art on view at the Museum.

_**[Purchase your Adult ticket online and receive a $1 discount.](https://everson.org/festival-of-trees-and-light/)**_ 

## At the **Everson**

- [Install shot of "America 250: Rebels, Radicals, and Revolutionaries"](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/america-250-rebels-radicals-and-revolutionaries/)

 [Install shot of "America 250: Rebels, Radicals, and Revolutionaries"](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/america-250-rebels-radicals-and-revolutionaries/)

 ### [_America 250: Rebels, Radicals, and Revolutionaries_](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/america-250-rebels-radicals-and-revolutionaries/)

 The American story is a tangle of aspiration and contradiction, triumph and struggle, liberty and oppression. From the nation’s founding, rebels, radicals, and revolutionaries have shaped the course of American history, not only through acts of courage and innovation, but through challenging convention and questioning authority. This exhibition presents artists whose works reflect that journey, celebrating moments of courage and progress while also confronting inequity and inaction....

 [Read More ›](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/america-250-rebels-radicals-and-revolutionaries/)

- 

 ### [_Sincerely, Beato_](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/sincerely-beato/)

 We remember Beatrice Wood, who signed her pithy correspondence as “Beato,” for her cutting wit, outrageous stories, lustrous ceramics, and complex relationship with artist Marcel Duchamp, a leader of the Dada movement. Determined to resist the life her wealthy parents envisioned for her, Wood became a defining figure of New York City’s Dada scene, embracing the art movement that reveled in absurdity, nonsense, and humor....

 [Read More ›](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/sincerely-beato/)

- [Install shot of Julia Kunin Electric Dream Machines](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/julia-kunin-electric-dream-machines/)

 [Install shot of Julia Kunin Electric Dream Machines](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/julia-kunin-electric-dream-machines/)

 ### [_Julia Kunin: Electric Dream Machines_](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/julia-kunin-electric-dream-machines/)

 With their lustrous surfaces and evocative shapes, the ceramic works of Brooklyn-based artist Julia Kunin aim for maximum sensory overload. Kunin forges disparate influences like Art Nouveau, Surrealism, and queer abstraction into shimmering ceramic sculptures. For Kunin, discovery and free association reign supreme. Kunin’s mental process echoes her physical process, ping-ponging from one concept to the next....

 [Read More ›](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/julia-kunin-electric-dream-machines/)

- 

 ### [_New Works in Clay_](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/new-works-in-clay/)

 The Everson has a long history of working with important contemporary artists. Over the last 58 years, the Everson has produced solo exhibitions for Yoko Ono, Morris Louis, Joan Mitchell, Bill Viola, William Wegman, Carrie Mae Weems, and a host of artists who loom large on the world stage. No exhibition in the Everson's history can compare to New Works in Clay by Contemporary Painters and Sculptors, a 1976 exhibition that involved bringing well-known painters and sculptors to Syracuse to produce a body of work in ceramics. The project was the brainchild of Margie Hughto, who served as both a professor at Syracuse University and as a curator at the Everson....

 [Read More ›](https://everson.org/explore/current-exhibitions/new-works-in-clay/)

[See More](https://everson.org/exhibitions/)

metadata.title: Home - MoMA PS1
metadata.description: Artist-centered and community-driven, MoMA PS1 embraces boundary-breaking ideas and experimental practices. A place where audiences can encounter and engage with new art and perspectives, the institution has offered insight into artists’ worldviews for nearly 50 years. Driven by a commitment to realizing artists’ visions, our programs explore the ways in which creative expression can inspire connection.

## Plan a Visit

See works by modern and contemporary masters in the Nasher's light-filled galleries and serene outdoor sculpture garden. Learn more about what to expect during your visit. 

[Plan a Visit](https://www.nashersculpturecenter.org/visit/plan-a-vist)

[FREE admission](https://www.nashersculpturecenter.org/programs-events/programs-list/program/id/277) during _Free First Saturdays_ every month!

## Free First Saturdays

Look, learn and love your time at the Nasher every first Saturday of the month. Bring the whole crew to create, discover and make new memories together. Each month features a rotating schedule of things to see and do.

[Learn More](https://www.nashersculpturecenter.org/programs-events/programs-list/program/id/277)

## Nasher Prize

Established in 2015, the Nasher Prize is an award dedicated exclusively to excellence in contemporary sculpture. Winners of the Nasher Prize embody the tenets of the award: to recognize a living artist whose body of work has had an extraordinary impact on our understanding of sculpture.  

[Learn More](https://www.nashersculpturecenter.org/programs-events/nasher-prize)

EXPLORE THE HUNTINGTON MUSEUM OF ART! Photo by Sa-Rai Robinette [See All Current Exhibits](https://hmoa.org/current-exhibitions/) The Huntington Museum of Art is located at 2033 McCoy Road in Huntington, W.Va. 

HMA hours are 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Tuesdays; 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Wednesdays through Saturdays; and noon to 5 p.m. Sundays. HMA is closed to the public on Mondays. 

Free Tuesdays at HMA are generously presented by the City of Huntington Mayor’s Council for the Arts. 

## DISCOVER NATURE HERE

## Plant Conservatory

Home to **West Virginia’s only plant conservatory**, our mission to cultivate the appreciation of nature really blooms inside the museum among the species of hundreds of beautiful, agricultural, and exotic plants.

[Learn More](https://hmoa.org/nature/)

## Hiking Trails

Our **six hiking trails** are well-marked and maintained, covering over 40 acres of woodland hillside on various inclines that lead to rich gardens, beautiful views, and exploration of the art of nature just outside of our doors.

[Learn More](https://hmoa.org/hiking-trails/)

## CLASSES & WORKSHOPS

The Huntington Museum of Art offers classes in a variety of subjects throughout the year. There are classes available for all ages and skill levels.

[Learn More](https://hmoa.org/classes-workshops/)

# Visit Renwick

### Address and Hours

Photo by Albert Ting

### Admission is Always Free

The Renwick Gallery is located near the White House and presents craft and decorative art from the Museum’s collection. The museum is open daily except December 25.

Renwick Gallery

Pennsylvania Avenue at 17th Street, NW

Washington, DC 20006

Hours

Mon - Sun:

10​:00 am‑5​:30 pm 

### Getting Here

The Renwick Gallery is located steps from the White House in the heart of historic federal Washington.The Renwick Gallery is a twenty-five minute walk from the [Smithsonian American Art Museum](https://americanart.si.edu/visit/saam), which shares its space with the National Portrait Gallery. 

#### Public Transit

The closest Metro stations are Farragut West (Blue, Orange, and Silver lines) and Farragut North (Red line). Barrier-free ramp access is available at the 17th Street entrance.

#### Parking

There is limited on-street parking at meters; several [paid parking garages are available in the neighborhood](https://d26w5x2gnqeqql.cloudfront.net/index.html?ui-components=header%2Cfooter%2Ctime-picker%2Cmap&destination-longitude=-77.039067&utm-source=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.si.edu%2Fmuseums%2Frenwick-gallery&title-override-text=Book%20Parking%20near%20the%20Smithsonian%20Renwick%20Gallery&affiliate-code=915&destination-latitude=38.899137).

### Common FAQs

Frequently asked and answered questions about visiting the Renwick Gallery. 

What is the closest Metro stop to the Renwick Gallery?

[The Renwick Gallery](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Renwick+Gallery+of+the+Smithsonian+American+Art+Museum/@38.901718,-77.0450068,14.34z/data=!3m1!5s0x89b7b7bc7f1249ff:0xff95595ec742875b!4m12!1m6!3m5!1s0x0:0x7990cc4f370b2161!2sRenwick+Gallery+of+the+Smithsonian+American+Art+Museum!8m2!3d38.89911!4d-77.0390607!3m4!1s0x0:0x7990cc4f370b2161!8m2!3d38.89911!4d-77.0390607) is located on Pennsylvania Avenue at 17th Street NW. The closest Metro stations are Farragut West (Blue, Orange, and Silver lines) and Farragut North (Red line).

Are tickets required to visit the Renwick Gallery?

No, tickets are not required to visit the Renwick Gallery of the Smithsonian American Art Museum. 

Are there tours of the Renwick Gallery?

Renwick offers walk-in tours from 12 to 1 p.m. and 2 to 3 p.m. daily. All walk-in tours are subject to volunteer docent availability and last-minute cancellations may occur.

Can I bring my stroller to the Renwick Gallery?

Yes, please use the ramp on 17th Street to enter. Occasionally, special exhibitions may limit stroller access during busy times.

Can I take photographs at the Renwick Gallery?

Handheld photography and video for personal use is generally encouraged throughout the museum. Sometimes, photography of particular artworks may not be allowed in selected special exhibitions; please check the wall signage to confirm. No tripods, selfie sticks, or similar long tools are permitted in the galleries to protect the artworks.

[Read Visitor Guidelines](https://americanart.si.edu/visit/guidelines)

### Accessibility

[Learn More](https://americanart.si.edu/visit/accessibility)

Barrier-free access to the museum is available at the 17th Street entrance. All areas of the building are served by elevators. Accessible restrooms are located throughout the museum. More information about [accessibility at the museum](https://americanart.si.edu/visit/accessibility), including services for visitors who have vision and/or hearing loss.

##### Social Narratives

Social narratives are designed to help prepare visitors for situations they may encounter at the Smithsonian museums. They address what to expect, museum rules and routines, safety information, and more.

- Visit Renwick [English](https://d3ec1vt3scx7rr.cloudfront.net/files/documents/2026-06/Renwick-Social-Narrative-2026_0.pdf) - [Español](https://d3ec1vt3scx7rr.cloudfront.net/files/documents/2026-06/Renwick-Narrativa-Social-espan%CC%83ol-2026.pdf)

Where is the entrance to the Renwick Gallery? Is there an accessible entrance at the Renwick Gallery?

The main entrance to the Renwick Gallery, accessible by a set of stairs and wide double-doors, is located on Pennsylvania Avenue. [Access via an accessible ramp](https://americanart.si.edu/visit/accessibility) is available at the 17th Street entrance.

Are there accessible restrooms at the Renwick Gallery?

At the Renwick Gallery, accessible restrooms are located on all levels with unisex accessible restrooms on the first floor and basement level.

Are service animals welcome at the museum?

Service animals are welcome at Smithsonian museums. Under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), a service animal is defined as a dog that has been individually trained to do work or perform tasks for an individual with a disability. 

### Shopping

The Renwick Gallery of the Smithsonian American Art Museum and the Renwick Gallery Store are open. Shop for unique gifts inspired by the collection and special exhibitions. 

Selected merchandise is available at the SAAM Museum Store and [online](https://saamnpgstore.si.edu/).

[Learn More](https://americanart.si.edu/visit/renwick/store)

# Whitney Western Art Museum

# Whitney Western Art Museum

## A Must-See Western Art Museum

**The Whitney Western Art Museum ranks among the finest Western art museums in the nation. Its galleries feature masterpieces by Frederic Remington, Charles M. Russell, Thomas Moran, Albert Bierstadt, and other influential artists, both traditional and contemporary. Just minutes from Yellowstone, the Whitney invites visitors to explore the powerful connections between art, history, and the American West. Wander through world-class galleries, take in timeless paintings and sculptures, and see how artists shaped the way the world imagines the West. Recognized by _Newsweek_ as one of the nation’s best art museums in its Readers’ Choice Awards, the Whitney is an essential stop on the road to Yellowstone.**

[Meet the Curators](https://centerofthewest.org/explore/western-art/meet-the-staff/)

[Frequently Asked Questions](https://centerofthewest.org/explore/western-art/f-a-q/)

[Explore Our Online Database](https://collections.centerofthewest.org/argus/bbhc/Portal/bbhc.aspx)

## Explore Our Digital Guide

The Whitney has an awesome **[digital guide](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001l4eHWOWsd1s5VfpBXW3wbWhUFGhz7qRNWY1_iciGk4PjR7V2olKL0dGkpvMvbIZBvcHlCGtpQmzMxj4_i32xo4pF1l252Q3nGibAhctwBEO6j20wLVn3doAqHuxJovuabw-_fQP-Ms88fc4y3WauejRiq5MYlYHs3WWPEjkiiTxhZJfRsh0Srg==&c=FcPDRykhoTk0BP9wR7FWA9BwIQ4BeBzssGb3dY8I7aH3Xm6ibGKndQ==&ch=q3I-6rLArUiU2oJtE0fXkVNmCYski8risDUfeNH2wkbb_tedCtJ25A==),** accessible through Bloomberg Connects, a free arts and culture app created by Bloomberg Philanthropies. Visitors—in person here in the Whitney or from anywhere in the world—can access the our world-class art collection and special exhibitions through the app. The Whitney was the first museum in Wyoming to join the app, which features free digital guides to more than 250 museums, galleries, gardens, and other cultural spaces around the world.

[INSTRUCTIONS TO DOWNLOAD & USE THE GUIDE](https://centerofthewest.org/whitney-digital-guide/)

## Peter Hassrick Public Programs

The Whitney Western Art Museum’s Peter Hassrick Public Programs series, named in honor of the late renowned western American art scholar Peter H. Hassrick, presents engaging and creative educational talks that align with Peter’s principal scholarly interest in 19th and early 20th century American art of the West. Find details about the series, videos of past programs, and information on Peter’s legacy by clicking the button below. Once we have upcoming programs scheduled, you’ll find them there as well.

[LEARN MORE ABOUT THE PETER HASSRICK PUBLIC PROGRAMS](https://centerofthewest.org/peter-hassrick-public-programs/)

## Whitney Gallery Themes

The Whitney Western Art Museum explores the real and mythic West through wildlife, landscapes, Native Americans, heroes and legends, and historic events.

[VISIT WHITNEY EXHIBITS](https://centerofthewest.org/explore/western-art/exhibits/)

## What Will You See?

Artworks in the Whitney—by the western masters and contemporary artists of today—may inspire you, intrigue you, entertain you. Here are a few highlights.

[SEE WHITNEY ARTWORK](https://centerofthewest.org/our-museums/western-art/whitney-museum-see/)

The Whitney has again been voted one of the “[**Best Art Museums**](https://www.newsweek.com/readerschoice/best-art-museum-2025)” by _Newsweek_! In this Readers’ Choice contest, expert panelists from the art world select ten nominees and readers vote on the winner. We’re in good company, second on a list that also includes the Art Institute of Chicago, the National Gallery of Art, and the MET. Congratulations to the Whitney for well-deserved recognition of exceptional dedication and contribution to the art world.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.newsweek.com/readerschoice/best-art-museum-2025)

@graph.description: The Buffalo Bill Center of the West, located in Cody, Wyoming, is a world-renowned Smithsonian Affiliate dedicated to preserving the rich heritage of the American West. The Center houses five unique museums under one roof celebrating history, culture, art, natural science, and more, and offers a range of immersive experiences including chuckwagon dinners, live raptors, special events, and customized exclusive tours. With its diverse collections, the Center serves as a focal point for exploration, discovery, and hands-on education.

 Discover the stories behind Louisiana's architectural heritage! Visit [https://www.facebook.com/louisianaarch](https://www.facebook.com/louisianaarch) for tickets.

 Recognized as the 2025 Humanities Documentary Film of the Year by the Louisiana Endowment for the Humanities! 

 Wednesday, November 11, 2026

 Alexandria Museum of Art, 933 2nd St., Alexandria, LA

 Presented in partnership with the Louisiana Architecture Foundation and AIA Central Louisiana. 

 Join us for an evening of history, architecture, and storytelling!

headings.text: Alexandria Museum of Art Keep On Creating
Stay Connected with AMoA! Be the first to know what’s happening at the Alexandria Museum of Art. Sign up for our emails to receive updates on upcoming exhibitions, events, programs, and more!
The Alexandria Museum of Art fosters a healthy and culturally rich community by embracing change and using the power of art to educate, inspire and heal.
Become a member of AMoA today.

# Brunnier Art Museum

- [Visit](https://museums.iastate.edu/visit)
- [Anderson Sculpture Garden](https://museums.iastate.edu/anderson-sculpture-garden)
- [Brunnier Art Museum](https://museums.iastate.edu/brunnier-art-museum)
- [Christian Petersen Art Museum](https://museums.iastate.edu/christian-petersen-art-museum)
- [Farm House Museum](https://museums.iastate.edu/farm-house-museum)
- [Art on Campus Map](https://arcg.is/Dbu4f0)

Seventeenth-century Venetian glass. Porcelain from imperial China. Jade carvings so intricate you'll wonder how anyone made them by hand. The Brunnier Art Museum is where craft meets design meets "I had no idea this was five minutes from my dorm."

For 50 years, we've been caring for, collecting, and exhibiting truly world-class art that supports learning at Iowa State and in our community. We're the only accredited museum in Iowa focused on decorative arts collection, and we're **open to everyone, for free.**  

Indulge your curiosity with something real: explore the galleries and take notice of the details, the light, and the effect it has on you. Come see for yourself.

## Explore the Brunnier Art Museum

- [Current exhibitions](https://museums.iastate.edu/exhibitions)
- [Calendar of events and closures](https://museums.iastate.edu/calendar-events)

### Hours of operation

Free parking is available in lot B1 north of the Scheman Building. There are two reserved spaces for museum visitors directly in front of the north set of doors into the Scheman Building. Handicap parking, with a state permit, is provided in lot B1.

### Accessibility

The main entrance to the [Scheman Building](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Scheman+Building/@42.021491,-93.6393147,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x87ee709de30c19e7:0xdca27c0d99cb8ebc!8m2!3d42.021491!4d-93.6367398!16s%2Fg%2F11c1n91d9x?entry=ttu) (north side) is accessible for those with mobility aids: accessible parking spaces, one set of automatic doors, and elevators inside.

[General visitor info](https://museums.iastate.edu/visit 'Visit')  

## History of the Brunnier Art Museum

Iowa State University President James H. Hilton (1953–1965) dreamed of a new Iowa State Center to expand outreach education, the arts, athletics, and housing. Beginning in 1959, alumni and friends funded the project, and in 1962 Ann and Henry Brunnier joined the effort.

Henry Brunnier donated stock to the building fund, while Ann promised to give a large collection of dolls and decorative arts. Although his gift was initially seen as more significant, hers proved more enduring. When her collection arrived in 1974, it filled two semi-truck trailers and totaled over 30,000 objects. The Scheman Continuing Education Building, including the Brunnier Galleries, opened on September 19, 1975.

Since 1961 when Henry and Ann Brunnier gifted their collections to Iowa State University, over 600 other private patrons have contributed more than 28,000 objects to expand the University Museums’ permanent collections. The Lagerstrom Collection, left to the university in a will, added many European and American decorative arts. Other collections have grown consistently as gifts were made over time, such as the W. Allen Perry Collection of Asian Arts, the Joyce Tomlison Brewer Collection of Native American Arts and the Iowa Artists Collection.

## Today

The Brunnier Art Museum is the only accredited museum in Iowa focused on decorative arts. It is also one of the few museums in the country inside a [performing arts and conference complex](https://www.center.iastate.edu/). Founded in 1975, the museum is named for its donors, Henry J. Brunnier and his wife Ann. See ceramics, glass, dolls, ivory, jade, and enameled metals in the Brunnier Art Collection.

The permanent collection includes prints, paintings, sculptures, textiles, carpets, wood, lacquered objects, silver, and furniture. The regularly changing exhibitions, from the permanent collection or a visiting collection, provide educational opportunities for all ages. The museum also hosts lectures, classes, panel discussions, and gallery walks that help visitors understand the art.

## [Graven Image. Aaron Spangler](https://ndmoa.com/graven-image/)

### November 5, 2026 – January 18, 2027

_Graven Image_ features the work of artist Aaron Spangler who has garnered regional and national recognition for championing and critiquing the ethos of rural life. _Graven Image_ highlights the sculptor’s versatility by including his large-scale woodblock prints and his monumental tapestries, as well as his freestanding carved and painted wood sculptures and bas-relief tableaux. 

[View](https://ndmoa.com/graven-image/)

## [Book Launch. NDMOA Permanent Collection Highlights, 2009–2025](https://ndmoa.com/book-launch/)

### November 5, 2026 – January 4, 2027

The upcoming publication will feature over 170 artworks that the Museum has collected between 2009 and 2025. To celebrate its release, this exhibition highlights some of the works featured in the upcoming catalog with an emphasis on pieces that have not been recently displayed in the Museum’s galleries. The _Permanent Collection Highlights_ catalog is slated to be released in early December.

[View](https://ndmoa.com/book-launch/)

## [Micah Bloom. Multifarious.](https://ndmoa.com/micah-bloom/)

### Currently on display

This collection of images represents Bloom’s eclectic creative production throughout the past 15 -20 years. It includes works from various projects and series and loosely functions as a retrospective of his artistic output while living in North Dakota (2011 present).

[View](https://ndmoa.com/micah-bloom/)

- We promise to connect the contemporary past and present by preserving and exhibiting art.

- We promise to enrich the community through interactive experiences and creative exchange.
- We promise to collaborate with community partners.
- We promise to be a social and intellectual hub for the community to create a sense of place.

# Nora Eccles Harrison Museum of Art

There is something for everyone... family friendly, free and open to the public, with free parking available!

[Events and Programs](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/index.php)

[Exhibitions](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/exhibitions/index.php)

[Collections](https://artmuseum-collection.usu.edu/)

[Education](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/education/index.php)

## Events

[Stories from Behind the Lens](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/michael-childers-event.php)

[Read Story](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/michael-childers-event.php)

## [Stories from Behind the Lens](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/michael-childers-event.php)

Join legendary photographer Michael Childers for an evening of stories, insights, and behind-the-scenes experiences from a career spent documenting some of the most influential figures in music, film, and popular culture.

[Beyond the Book](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/beyond-the-book.php)

[Read Story](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/beyond-the-book.php)

## [Beyond the Book](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/beyond-the-book.php)

Join Camille Mortensen for Beyond the Book, a quarterly book club where great books spark meaningful conversations and connection.

[Community Art Day](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/community-art-days.php)

[Read Story](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/community-art-days.php)

## [Community Art Day](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/community-art-days.php)

Second Saturday of Every Month 
10:00 AM - 1:30 PM @ NEHMA 

Learn about and make art! Free and open to all.

[Mini Makers Toddler Art Exploration Program](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/mini-makers.php)

[Read Story](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/mini-makers.php)

## [Mini Makers Toddler Art Exploration Program](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/mini-makers.php)

Join us for Mini Makers class, where caregivers and toddlers ages 2-5 experience art through singing, playing, moving, and making. $5/child and prior registration is required.

[Nights at NEHMA](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/NightsatNEHMA.php)

[Read Story](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/NightsatNEHMA.php)

## [Nights at NEHMA](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/NightsatNEHMA.php)

Visit NEHMA’s Wanlass Center for Art Education and Research on first Friday evenings for art-making, date-nights, scavenger hunts, and more! Free and open to all.

[The Creative Reset](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/the-creative-reset.php)

[Read Story](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/the-creative-reset.php)

## [The Creative Reset](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/the-creative-reset.php)

Relieve your stress! Join us on Fridays to make and decorate hand-made books using collage, mixed media, printing, drawing, and painting. Try new art processes inspired by artists in the collection as you look around NEHMA’s Object Study Room in the new W...

[View More Events](https://www.usu.edu/artmuseum/events/index.php)

## Visit

Come experience what’s on display at the museum! For information on program offerings, visit our [event calendar](https://museum.wsu.edu/calendar/). 

Open hours are Tuesday through Saturdays from 10am to 4pm, CLOSED Sunday, Monday, holidays and university breaks including Thanksgiving Break: closing 11/26/26, reopening 12/1/26, and Winter Break: closing 12/13/26, reopening 1/12/27.

[Visit the Museum](https://museum.wsu.edu/visit/)

## Exhibitions & Programs

You can explore our current, upcoming, and past exhibitions online. Each year the museum hosts six to ten exhibitions, often showcasing art of all mediums, by local and national artists.

[Explore Exhibitions](https://museum.wsu.edu/exhibitions-events/)

## Collections

There are over 4,000 works of art in our permanent collection, which we want to share with you. 

Check out our online database to explore the collection.

[Explore Collections](https://museum.wsu.edu/museum-collections/)

## Education & Tours

Looking to schedule a tour? We give tours for school groups K-12, college classes, and community organizations. Through our Buy-A-Bus program your K-12 school may be eligible for bus travel reimbursement.

[Education & Tours](https://museum.wsu.edu/education-highlights/)

## About JSMA WSU

Since 1974, the museum has dedicated itself to sharing the visual arts with the students, faculty and staff of WSU, to the local community, eastern Washington, and the nation.

[Learn About Us](https://museum.wsu.edu/about-us-2/)

## Support the Regional Art Experience

The museum’s mission is to combine academic needs with community connections to transform the regional art experience. This work would not be possible without our generous community of supporters. 

Learn about how you can support the arts in the Pacific Northwest.

[Support](https://museum.wsu.edu/support-the-museum/)

## [In the News](https://museum.wsu.edu/about-us/news/)

## Events

_WSU Pullman is located on the ceded lands of the Nimíipuu (Nez Perce) Tribe and the traditional homelands of the Palus Band of Indians. We acknowledge their presence here since time immemorial and recognize their continuing connection to the land, to the water, and to their ancestors._ 

[WSU's land acknowledgement](https://wsu.edu/about/land-acknowledgement/)

[Back To Top](https://museum.wsu.edu/#top)

## HOURS

# The Latest at Museum of Glass

## Here’s what you need to know.

### [Capital Renovation Grand Opening](https://www.museumofglass.org/grandopening)

Ribbon cutting and the _Lino Tagliapietra Legacy Gallery |_ December 12

Join Museum of Glass on **Saturday**, **December 12** as we celebrate the grand opening and ribbon cutting of our new museum spaces! This event commemorates the conclusion of our transformational [capital renovation project](https://www.museumofglass.org/2026), the reopening of our galleries, and the debut of the [_Lino Tagliapietra Legacy Gallery_](https://www.museumofglass.org/ltlg), featuring its first exhibition [_Lino Tagliapietra: Maestro_](https://www.museumofglass.org/lino)_._

**The ribbon cutting will begin at 10:30am** with light bites and remarks from Museum and local leadership and the gallery’s curator Susan Warner. Docent tours of [_Lino Tagliapietra: Maestro_](https://www.museumofglass.org/lino) will be available throughout the day.

[**Learn more and get tickets →**](https://www.museumofglass.org/grandopening)

### [Lino Tagliapietra Celebration Week](https://www.museumofglass.org/lino-week)

January 20-24

With the new gallery spaces and _Lino Tagliapietra Legacy Gallery_ opening on December 12, Museum of Glass invites you to a special week of programming honoring the legacy gallery’s cornerstone artist! The Museum Hot Shop will feature a different artist from Lino’s glassblowing team every day, demonstrating the techniques and inspirations they have gained from years of working with Lino. A special artist panel with the artists and _Lino Tagliapietra Legacy Gallery_ curator Susan Warner will be held on Saturday, January 23 at 1pm, where they will discuss Lino’s career and his unparalleled impact on glassmaking in the Pacific Northwest.

[**Learn more and get tickets →**](https://www.museumofglass.org/lino-week)

### [**Fireside: A Holiday Night at Museum of Glass**](https://www.museumofglass.org/fireside)

December 19 | 5-9pm

Join Museum of Glass for a festive holiday evening featuring hands-on workshops, crafts, and gallery tours! Outside on the Museum’s Grand Plaza, enjoy the lights from the [Tacoma Yacht Club Lighted Boat Parade](https://www.tacomayachtclub.org/Public_Events/Lighted_Boat_Parade). Inside the Museum, explore the new exhibition [_Lino Tagliapietra: Maestro_](https://www.museumofglass.org/lino) through docent-led tours, watch flameworking and glassblowing demos in the Grand Hall and Hot Shop, create your own works of art in glass in one of our Glass Pendant Workshops or By the Furnace: Hot Shop Experience sessions, and more. Fireside will also feature a holiday market featuring local artisans and vendors where you can pick up any last minute gifts before the holidays.

[**Tickets to Fireside →**](https://www.museumofglass.org/fireside)

## [2026 Museum of Glass Capital Project](https://www.museumofglass.org/2026)

Since its founding nearly 25 years ago, Museum of Glass has become a cultural icon in the Pacific Northwest, and a place where imagination, artistry, and innovation thrive. Now, it is time for the Museum to embrace a larger role.

### In April of 2026, **Museum of Glass embarked on the first capital renovation project in its history. During construction, all Museum traditional gallery spaces will be closed. The Museum will reopen its gallery spaces on December 12, 2026.**

The Museum needs to modernize, improve, and expand its gallery spaces to present a more thorough, interdisciplinary perspective on the art form, celebrate its pioneering artists, and exhibit more work from emerging and established artists. A foundational component of this expansion is a new immersive gallery dedicated to the Lino Tagliapietra collection—175 works, recently gifted to the Museum from the artist.  

[Learn More About the Project →](https://www.museumofglass.org/2026)

# In the Galleries

## Learn more about the exhibitions currently on view.

### [_Lino Tagliapietra Legacy Gallery_](https://www.museumofglass.org/ltlg)

Museum of Glass became a collecting institution in 2007. Since that time, it has built a significant collection of works by artists who have completed residencies in the Hot Shop, glass pieces that document the Studio Glass movement, contemporary glass, and nineteenth- and early twentieth-century glass produced in factories in the United States and Europe. However, the Museum’s collection has not yet been able to tell a sufficiently comprehensive story of glass and the Pacific Northwest’s critical role in its advancement. Until now. Lino Tagliapietra, the world’s most renowned living glass _maestro_, has generously gifted 175 works and installations from his archival collection to Museum of Glass.

**As part of the** [**Museum of Glass 2026 capital renovation project**](https://www.museumofglass.org/2026)**, Museum of Glass is building the immersive new** [**_Lino Tagliapietra Legacy Gallery_**](https://www.museumofglass.org/ltlg)**_,_ scheduled to open in the December 12, 2026.**

[Learn More About What's Coming to Our Galleries →](https://www.museumofglass.org/ltlg)

# Enhance Your Experience

## Take a guided tour, participate in workshops, and visit the Museum Hot Shop.

[Check Out the Latest Opportunities →](https://www.museumofglass.org/calendar-of-events)

[Hot Shop workshops at Museum of Glass](https://www.museumofglass.org/workshops)

### [Make Your Own Art](https://www.museumofglass.org/workshops)

Learn how to create your own glass art in a variety of hands-on workshops inspired by the Museum’s current exhibitions, the season, events, and more. 

Details on available workshops is available [here](https://www.museumofglass.org/workshops).

[Tours at Museum of Glass](https://www.museumofglass.org/group-school-tours)

### [Take a Tour](https://www.museumofglass.org/group-school-tours)

Add a docent-led tour to your next visit to MOG and get an personal and interactive experience in the galleries. Want to really stretch your legs? Consider an outdoor walking tour and learn about the art and architecture on the Thea Foss Waterway.

[Glassblowing in Museum of Glass Hot Shop](https://www.museumofglass.org/visiting-artist-lineup)

### [See Who’s in the Hot Shop](https://www.museumofglass.org/visiting-artist-lineup)

The Museum’s **Visiting Artist Residency Program** hosts artists in our world-class Hot Shop to create new works in glass with our Hot Shop Team. These artists create a sense of excitement and wonder as they experiment and explore new directions in their art that may not be possible in their own studios. 

[Home Gallery](https://www.museumofglass.org/#new-gallery) [MOG Home Page](https://www.museumofglass.org/#mog-home-page)

_Museum of Glass acknowledges and is grateful to be located on the traditional homelands of the Puyallup Tribe and Coast Salish peoples. The Puyallup people have lived on and stewarded these lands since the beginning of time and continue to do so today. We recognize that this land acknowledgement is one small step toward meaningful allyship and will continue to build inclusive and respectful partnerships to amplify the voices, experiences, and histories of these communities._

# The Hallie Ford Museum of Art

Embracing the creativity of the human spirit as expressed in the art of different cultures, places and times.

- Handmade Revolution: Craft in the Pacific Northwest

 June 13, 2026 – March 13, 2027 | Maribeth Collins Lobby and Melvin Henderson-Rubio Gallery

 [More Information](https://hfma.willamette.edu/exhibitions/library/2026-27/handmade-revolution.html 'Handmade Revolution: Craft in the Pacific Northwest')

- Drawn from the Collection

 [More Information](https://hfma.willamette.edu/exhibitions/library/2026-27/drawn-from-the-collection.html 'Drawn from the Collection Exhibition Details')

- What Do We Hold? A Community Conversation

 July 11 to November 21, 2026 | James Nafziger Gallery

 [More Information](https://hfma.willamette.edu/exhibitions/library/2026-27/what-we-hold.html 'What Do We Hold? A Community Conversation Exhibition Information')

## HOURS OF OPERATION

**Normal Hours:** Tuesday-Saturday  |  Noon to 5 p.m.

---

## About the Museum

The only liberal arts college art museum in the Northwest, the museum is located near the Oregon State Capitol in the heart of Salem, Oregon. The museum is a leader in the research on the art of the Northwest, with one of the most significant collections of Northwest art and a history of important publications and exhibitions. The [museum’s collections](https://hfma.willamette.edu/collections/index.html) reflect the rich [Pacific Northwest](https://hfma.willamette.edu/collections/pacific-nw/index.html) culture and explore the history of art around the world.

[Special exhibitions](https://hfma.willamette.edu/exhibitions/index.html) range from classical works to modern masters, while the permanent galleries feature works by Pacific Northwest and Native American artists as well as a diverse collection of Ancient, European, American, and Asian art. 

[Read the Director's Message](https://hfma.willamette.edu/about/from-director.html) [Meet the Staff](https://hfma.willamette.edu/about/staff/index.html) [Museum History](https://hfma.willamette.edu/about/index.html)

Tacoma Art Museum is located on the homelands of the Puyallup Tribe of Indians. We recognize and honor the enduring Puyallup people and Coast Salish communities as we strive for a fuller understanding of the histories and currents of this place, and a more equitable future. Jean-Léon Gérôme (French, 1824–1904), _Sketch for Le derviche tourneur (The Whirling Dervish) \[detail\]_, 1899, oil on paper mounted on canvas, 9 x 12 1/2 inches. Collection of Middlebury College Museum of Art. Purchase with funds provided by the Christian A. Johnson Memorial Art Acquisition Fund, 2014.019. (Photo: May Mantell, Vermont)

The Middlebury College Museum of Art is the largest learning laboratory on campus and a vibrant cultural hub in the local and regional community. Our expansive collections and diverse temporary loan exhibits provide opportunities for all visitors to be engaged and inspired.

## Come to the Purchase Party!

Saturday, November 7, 5:00pm, Kirk Alumni Center. Three students working with Sarah Rogers will present three works of art for possible purchase, and YOU get to vote to determine which gets added to the collection. Enjoy dinner from the Arab world and a beer/wine bar (each ticket includes one free drink).

[**Get your tickets**](http://midd.art/purchase26)

## Two Greek Vases, Reattributed

### New Scholarship Clarifies the Origins of Two Lekythoi

Professor of History of Art and Architecture Pieter Broucke details recent research that led to definitive artist attributions for two vases in Middlebury’s Collection.

### [The Friends’ First Acquisition, Revisited](https://midd.art/marathon)

The first object Middlebury’s Friends of the Art Museum ever gifted to the museum, upon their founding in 1969, was an Ancient Greek black-figure white-ground lekythos decorated by a then unknown artist. Last spring, however, two scholars identified the painter of this vase.

[Read about the Marathon Painter vase](https://midd.art/marathon)

### [A Related Vase, Also Reattributed](https://midd.art/aischines)

In 2010, the museum acquired a red-figure white-ground lekythos meant to complement the black-figure lekythos. This more recent acquisition has a fascinating provenance, and it, too, has been newly reattributed.

[Read about the Aischines Painter vase](https://midd.art/aischines)

 Play

### Campus Public Art Walking Tour: An Introduction

An introduction to a walking tour of Middlebury’s public art collection, narrated by Professor Emeritus of History of Art and Architecture John Hunisak.

## Friends of the Art Museum

Each year, members help shape the Museum’s collection, support learning opportunities, and enjoy access to programs that connect people and ideas through the visual arts. Friends’ dues drive acquisitions which are selected annually at the Museum’s Purchase Party. Dues also enable student participation at member events and allow the Museum to pursue exciting and engaging speakers, performers, and artists. Join us as a Friend today.

[Become a Member](https://www.middlebury.edu/museum/support/friends-art-museum)

## Visit Us

The museum serves as an integral [educational and cultural component](https://www.middlebury.edu/museum/teaching-learning) of Middlebury College yet also seeks to enrich the larger educational and cultural environment of Vermont.

More about [planning your visit](https://www.middlebury.edu/museum/visit).

### Asian Art at Dartmouth Highlights from the Hood Museum of Art

_Asian Art at Dartmouth: Highlights from the Hood Museum of Art_ showcases key works of Asian art from the Hood Museum across many mediums. The exhibition's overview of the collection encompasses historical works from Japan, Korea, China, the Tibetan and Himalayan Plateau, and South and Southeast Asia, as well as selected examples of contemporary art by Asian artists working around the globe.

# Dia Beacon

Riggio Galleries 
3 Beekman Street, Beacon, New York

Dia Beacon, Riggio Galleries, Beacon, New York. Photo: Bill Jacobson Studio, New York

# Hours

3 Beekman Street 
Beacon, New York

Friday–Monday, 10 am–4 pm (hours change seasonally)

Please arrive before 3:30 pm for admission. 

Dia Beacon is closed Tuesday–Thursday, as well as on Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day.

The cafe is open Friday–Monday, 9:45 am–3:45 pm; indoor and outdoor seating is available. The Shop is open Friday–Monday, 10 am–4 pm.

On-site parking is limited. On busy weekends and holidays, additional parking may be available at the Beacon train station.

# Admission

Admission 
$25 Adults 
$18 Seniors 65+ 
$12 Students 
$12 Visitors with disabilities 
$5 Children 5–11 

Free for Dia members, children under 5, care partners of visitors with disabilities, and Beacon and Newburgh residents.

Advance reservations are suggested, but not required. Get tickets [here](https://diaart.org/visit/tickets). 

For groups of 10 or more, schedule a visit [here](https://www.diaart.org/learning/guided-tours-and-group-visits).

[Become a member today](https://www.diaart.org/support/membership) to receive free admission to Dia Beacon, discounts at our shops, access to special events, and more. 

Dia accepts credit and debit cards, mobile payments and cash.  

Dia Art Foundation is committed to welcoming all visitors to Dia Beacon. We honor reciprocal memberships and offer free admission for military families and veterans (plus one), SNAP participants, and EBT cardholders.

Beacon and Newburgh residents receive free admission.

Hudson Valley residents receive free admission on the last Sunday of each month.

To reserve free or discounted tickets, please fill out our [free admission request](https://diaart.wufoo.com/forms/dia-beacon-free-admission-reservations-request/ 'https://diaart.wufoo.com/forms/dia-beacon-free-admission-reservations-request/').

To request special accommodation or to ask questions about your visit, please contact 845 231 0811 or [tickets@diaart.org](mailto:tickets@diaart.org 'mailto:tickets@diaart.org'). 

If you are a member of the press, please contact [press@diaart.org](mailto:press@diaart.org) for more information about visiting. 

Dia is not able to refund or exchange admission tickets with less than a 24-hour notice.

### Visitor Guidelines

We look forward to welcoming you to Dia’s locations and sites! Please review our visitor guidelines before your visit.  

- Advance ticket reservations are suggested for Dia Beacon.
- Gallery attendants are available to assist you; please respect their guidance.
- Please keep a safe distance and do not touch the artwork.
- Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.
- Food and drinks (including water bottles) are not permitted in the galleries.
- Large bags and backpacks are not permitted in the galleries; a coat-and-bag check is available for visitor use. 
- Please note certain galleries may be closed or have limited access due to the nature of the work. 
- Groups of 10 or more should schedule their visit [here](https://www.diaart.org/learning/group-visits).

### Groups and Tours

**Group visits 
**Learning at Dia Art Foundation is founded on the idea that art is an active, self-determined experience.

Advance reservations are required for all adult and student groups. To schedule a group visit or guided tour, please visit our [group visits](https://www.diaart.org/learning/guided-tours-and-group-visits) page.

Dia Art Foundation strives to provide group tours to educational or other nonprofit groups regardless of means. Please ask for details when making a reservation. 

**Public tours 
**Dia Beacon provides public tours every Saturday and Sunday at 12 pm and 1:30 pm. Tours are free with admission; no reservation required.

**Guided walk-throughs of artworks 
**Walk-throughs of Michael Heizer’s _North, East, South, West_ (1967/2002) or Lawrence Weiner’s _CADMIUM & MUD & TITANIUM & LEAD & FERROUS OXIDE & SO ON . . ._ (1991) are offered at 9:30 am on museum open days. Walk-throughs are up to 30 minutes long and are limited to a maximum of 10 guests at a time. Requirements and conditions vary as outlined below.

Due to the nature of Michael Heizer’s artwork, guests must be 18 or older and are asked to refrain from photography.

Walk-throughs of Lawrence Weiner’s artwork take place outdoors and are offered weather permitting. Appropriate footwear is recommended, and guests under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.

Reservations are encouraged but not required. To reserve a spot, please provide your name, the number of guests, the day of your visit, and the artwork of interest via email to [morningtours@diaart.org](mailto:morningtours@diaart.org).

Please note Dia Beacon reserves the right to cancel walk-throughs for any reason. For questions or additional information, please call 845 231 0811.

_Morning walkthroughs are included in the cost of admission._

### Hudson Valley Free Day

Photo: Eva Deitch 

Hudson Valley residents receive free admission to Dia Beacon on the last Sunday of each month. The Hudson Valley encompasses the following counties: Albany, Columbia, Dutchess, Greene, Orange, Putnam, Rensselaer, Rockland, Saratoga, Schenectady, Sullivan, Ulster, Washington, and Westchester.

Additionally, City of Beacon and Newburgh residents receive free admission to Dia Beacon every day.

To get tickets in advance for Hudson Valley Free Day please fill out our [Free Admission Request](https://diaart.wufoo.com/forms/dia-beacon-free-admission-reservations-request/ 'https://diaart.wufoo.com/forms/dia-beacon-free-admission-reservations-request/').

Hudson Valley Free Days at Dia Beacon are made possible by Kiki McMillan, Charlie Pohlad, and the Pohlad family.

### Dia Beacon Landscape Project

Rendering courtesy of Studio Zwede

Dia Beacon has undergone a major landscaping project designed by landscape architect firm [Studio Zewde](https://www.studio-zewde.com/ 'https://www.studio-zewde.com/'). The South Garden will open an additional eight acres of Dia’s thirty-two-acre campus to the public. 

Construction began in summer 2024, with the South Garden opening to the public in 2027. More information on the project will be continually updated [on our blog](https://www.diaart.blog/landscape-project 'https://www.diaart.blog/landscape-project').

### Photography and Recording

- Unless otherwise noted, still and video photography for personal use is allowed at Dia sites, with a limit of 5 minutes in a given space; flash photography is not permitted.
- Wedding, engagement, or event photography is not allowed on Dia property.
- Commercial photography and the use of professional film or equipment (including tripods and extension poles) is not allowed without prior arrangement with Dia. 
- If you are uncertain about photography or filming at a Dia site, please ask Visitor Services staff.
- Use of the shared space must not be disruptive to other visitors; please respect Dia property and do not move, climb on, or damage furniture.
- Use of drones is not allowed on Dia property.

Dia Art Foundation reserves the right to prohibit still and video photography in any area at any time. Failure to adhere to these guidelines may result in visitors being asked to cease activities and/or leave the premises.

Images for educational use may be requested by contacting Dia’s Rights and Reproduction department at [rights@diaart.org](mailto:rights@diaart.org). For images for press, contact Dia’s Press department at [press@diaart.org](mailto:press@diaart.org). Enquire about professional/commercial photography at [rentals@diaart.org](mailto:rentals@diaart.org).

### Accessibility and Service Animals

Dia Beacon has accessible parking, galleries, and bathrooms, as well as elevators to all levels.

Wheelchairs are available for visitor use; reservations are not required.

ADA service dogs are welcome. Pets, including therapy or emotional-support animals, are not permitted in the galleries.

Certain galleries may be closed or have limited access due to the nature of the work. For questions about accessibility, please contact 845 231 0811 or [info@diaart.org](https://www.diaart.org/visit/visit-our-locations-sites/info@diaart.org).

### Library Membership Passes

Dia Art Foundation is pleased to partner with libraries to offer local communities unlimited access to our groundbreaking exhibitions and projects. Our Library membership program provides patrons of participating libraries a membership pass that grants free admission for up to six guests and for children ages 18 and under. Please visit our [Libraries](https://diaart.org/support/libraries) page for more information about our Library membership program. For further questions or assistance with enrollment, please contact 212 293 5520 or [membership@diaart.org](mailto:membership@diaart.org).

### Family Programs

Photo: Eva Deitch

Family programs at Dia invite people of all ages to exercise their creative agency through intergenerational, participatory, and playful artist-led engagements, both in the studio and in the galleries.

**[Saturday Studio](https://diaart.org/program/program/saturday-studio) 
**Join practicing artists for free workshops of art-making, material experimentation, and play. Designed for all ages, Saturday Studio is a family-friendly program that is most suitable for children ages five and up. All families participating in the Saturday Studio program receive free admission to Dia Beacon for the day.

**[Play Sets](https://diaart.org/program/program/play-sets/) 
**Explore the galleries through in-depth engagements with a single artist or artwork. Each program will include hands-on exercises that invite participants to see, think, and imagine in new ways. Recommended for families with children ages five and up.
