Dia Beacon has limited onsite parking. On busy weekends and holidays, drivers may be asked to park at the Metro-North Beacon Station, located 1/2 mile (approximately an 8-10 minute walk) away. 

# Shop and Cafe

Photo: Don Stahl

The Dia Beacon Shop is open Friday–Monday, 10 am–4 pm. The shop offers Dia publications; artist monographs; exhibition catalogs; publications on architecture, design, and writing; children’s books; regional titles; and periodicals. Dia publications are also available [online](https://shop.diaart.org/).

The Dia Beacon Cafe is open Friday–Monday, 9:45 am–3:45 pm. Operated by Mountain Provisions, the cafe offers a [seasonal menu](https://www.davethebutcherny.com/dia-beacon-cafe) of house-made soups, salads, and sandwiches, as well as local pastries, coffee, and espresso drinks. Indoor and outdoor seating is available. 

# About Dia Beacon

### Background

Occupying a former Nabisco box-printing factory on the banks of the Hudson River, Dia Beacon presents the majority of Dia’s collection of art from the 1960s to the present as well as special exhibitions, new commissions, and public and education programs. Since its opening in May 2003, Dia Beacon has helped transform the city of Beacon into a vibrant arts destination for visitors from the region, New York City, and beyond.  

**Architecture** 
Built in 1929 by Nabisco, the nearly 300,000-square-foot factory building is composed of brick, steel, concrete, and glass and is considered a landmark of early-twentieth-century industrial architecture. It stands as a symbol of Beacon’s past as a major industrial and manufacturing city. 

The original building had many key design elements that made it an appealing site for contemporary art, including broad spans between supporting columns and more than 34,000-square-feet of skylights. Today these skylights provide natural light in the galleries and have uniquely established Dia Beacon as a “daylight museum.”

Dia invited artist Robert Irwin to conceive the master plan for a twenty-first-century museum that retained the original character of the factory’s interior spaces. Irwin also designed seasonally changing gardens throughout the surrounding landscape. Following the renovation, Dia Beacon was added to the National Register of Historic Places. 

**Art and Programs** 
In keeping with Dia’s history of single-artist, site-related presentations, each gallery was designed specifically for the installation of one artist’s work. This attentiveness to the work becomes tangible when traversing the spaces at Dia Beacon, which were renovated to display, for example, Dan Flavin’s “monuments” for V. Tatlin(1964–90), Richard Serra’s Torqued Ellipses (1996–2000), and Michael Heizer’s _North, East, South, West_ (1967/2002). 

Dia’s collections and special presentations are supplemented by public programs, tours, and an arts education partnership with the City of Beacon, underway since 2001.

## Mint Museum Uptown

In the heart of Uptown Charlotte and an integral part of the Levine Center for the Arts, Mint Museum Uptown is home to our renowned Craft + Design collection. Permanent collections also include American Art, Modern and Contemporary Art, and Craft + Design, along with a rotating series featuring local artists, Constellation CLT.

[Uptown Visual Guide](https://www.mintmuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Uptown_Visual-Aid-Tour-1.pdf)

### Locations

**Mint Museum Uptown**

_Your General admission ticket gives you access to both Mint Museum Uptown and Mint Museum Randolph for two consecutive days._

### Admission

**Mint Members** – [Join today!](https://www.mintmuseum.org/membership/)

FREE

##### [Click here for our full list of admission discounts](https://www.mintmuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/The-Mint-Museum-Admission-Discounts.pdf)

Parking Uptown

Mint Museum Uptown offers $10 maximum validation before 5 PM Monday – Friday to our visitors in the \*Levine Center for the Arts parking garage located on Brooklyn Village Avenue between Tryon and Church Streets. If using GPS, you can enter address [**130 West Brooklyn Village Ave, Charlotte, NC 28202**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/TyG7TRdMZPYk8uX27) to find the garage entrance. \*When parking in the Levine Center of the Arts parking garage, we cannot guarantee there will be a parking spot if lot is full.

Parking is a flat fee of $10 after 5 PM and during the weekends.

[Driving Directions](https://goo.gl/maps/8fnP7CvsNGK215bh6) [Uptown parking guide](https://www.mintmuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/guide-to-getting-uptown.pdf)

## Mariposa at the Mint

World-to-table dining in the heart of Uptown Charlotte. Enjoy lunch, dinner, or weekend jazz brunch before or after exploring the museum.

[Learn more](https://www.mariposaclt.com/)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Where should I park?

Mint Museum Randolph offers a spacious parking lot directly in front of the building. Park for free!

Mint Museum Uptown offers $10 maximum validation before 5 PM Monday – Friday to our visitors in the \*Levine Center for the Arts parking garage located on Brooklyn Village Avenue between Tryon and Church Streets. If using GPS, you can enter address **130 West Brooklyn Village Ave, Charlotte, NC 28202** to find the garage entrance. \*When parking in the Levine Center of the Arts parking garage, we cannot guarantee there will be a parking spot if lot is full.

Parking is a flat fee of $10 after 5 PM and during the weekends.

Do you have any free admission nights?

Admission is free every Wednesday night from 5 – 9 PM at both the Mint Museum Randolph and the Mint Museum Uptown.

Is re-entry allowed?

Admission is good for two consecutive days at both Mint Museum Randolph and Mint Museum Uptown locations. Feel free to re-enter throughout the same day with your receipt.

How long does it take to visit the museum?

On average, the Mint Museum Randolph or Mint Museum Uptown will take roughly two to two-and-a-half hours to complete when special exhibitions are on display.

What type of Museum is the Mint?

The Mint Museum is a leading, innovative museum of international art and design committed to engaging and inspiring all members of our global community.

[Learn More](https://www.mintmuseum.org/about/)

What are your accessibility measures?

We are committed to making the museum accessible to all visitors. Please note that our efforts to make our website, buildings, galleries and programs more accessible are ongoing.

[Accessibility](https://www.mintmuseum.org/accessibility/)

Are bookbags allowed?

Bags measuring 11 x 17 x 5 inches or larger are not allowed in our galleries and must be stored in our complimentary lockers. Security officers and Guest Services may ask you to carry smaller bags on your front or by your side to ensure the safety of the artwork.

Do you have a coat check?

Yes, our coat check is open during winter months and during special occasions.

Can I visit the museum store without admission?

Yes, you may visit the stores at either location without admission.

Can I touch the art?

No. The touching of any works of art is strictly prohibited in order to best share art with the community for many years to come.

Are photos allowed?

Yes, we encourage photography of the art for personal use. No flash, selfie sticks, tripods, or photographing in restricted areas is allowed.

PLEASE NOTE: All interior photo shoots using the space for events (including but not limited to graduation, prom, engagement, and maternity) are subject to a $300/hour fee. [These requests must be made at least two weeks in advance. Availability of the requested spaces is not guaranteed.](https://mintmuseum.wufoo.com/forms/m4nb25j1enefzp/) 

All photography of a non-personal nature (i.e. editorial, commercial, advertisement) is prohibited without the permission of The Mint Museum.

Can I sketch inside the galleries?

Feel free to bring pencil and paper to sketch within our permanent collection galleries. Pens, markers, water, charcoal, pastels, paints, and easels are not allowed in the galleries. Some special exhibitions may have different rules.

Do you accept art donations?

We do not accept unsolicited art donations.

Do you do appraisal/conservation of works of art?

Unfortunately, we do not offer appraisal or conservation services.

Do you have restrooms?

Yes, restrooms are located on every floor for museum visitors who have purchased admission.

Is there a nursing room?

Yes, at Mint Museum Uptown. Please ask a guest services associate for assistance.

Are food and drinks allowed?

Food and drink are not allowed in the galleries under any circumstances.

Is smoking allowed?

The Mint Museum is a smoke-free institution.

Learn More

Accessibility

Bags measuring 11 x 17 x 5 inches or larger are not allowed in our galleries and must be stored in our complimentary lockers. Security officers and Guest Services may ask you to carry smaller bags on your front or by your side to ensure the safety of the artwork.

mainEntity.name: Do you have a coat check?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you may visit the stores at either location without admission.

All photography of a non-personal nature (i.e. editorial, commercial, advertisement) is prohibited without the permission of The Mint Museum.

## Mint Museum Randolph

Located in what was the first United States branch mint, it opened in Charlotte’s Eastover neighborhood as North Carolina’s first art museum. Permanent collection galleries include Art of the Ancient Americas, African Art, European Art, and Native American Art. This location also houses the Mint’s library, which contains over 23,000 books, 230 magazines, and 5,500 artist files.

[Driving directions](https://goo.gl/maps/iARz4HNdXktZfuBk7)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Where should I park?

Mint Museum Randolph offers a spacious parking lot directly in front of the building. Park for free!

Is there a good public transportation option for Mint Museum Randolph?

For the Charlotte Area Transportation System, use bus route 15 and 62x to bus stop Randolph Road and Museum Plaza which is within walking distance of Mint Museum Randolph

Do you have any free admission nights?

Play Related Audio

 Your browser does not support the audio element.

Admission is free every Wednesday night from 5 – 9 PM at both the Mint Museum Randolph and the Mint Museum Uptown.

Is re-entry allowed?

Admission is good for two consecutive days at both Mint Museum Randolph and Mint Museum Uptown locations. Feel free to re-enter throughout the same day with your receipt.

How long does it take to visit the museum?

On average, the Mint Museum Randolph or Mint Museum Uptown will take roughly two to two-and-a-half hours to complete when special exhibitions are on display.

What type of Museum is the Mint?

The Mint Museum is a leading, innovative museum of international art and design committed to engaging and inspiring all members of our global community.

[Learn More](https://www.mintmuseum.org/about/)

What are your accessibility measures?

We are committed to making the museum accessible to all visitors. Please note that our efforts to make our website, buildings, galleries and programs more accessible are ongoing.

[Accessibility at the Mint](https://www.mintmuseum.org/accessibility/)

Are bookbags allowed?

Bookbags and large heavy bags are not allowed inside the galleries. We have lockers at each location where these items can be stored during your visit.

Do you have a coat check?

Yes, our coat check is open during winter months and during special occasions. If it is closed, you may ask to leave your items with guest services behind the desk.

Can I visit the museum store without admission?

Yes, you may visit the stores at either location without admission.

Can I touch the art?

The touching of any works of art is strictly prohibited in order to best share art with the community for many years to come.

Are photos allowed?

Yes, we encourage photography for personal use. No flash, selfie sticks, tripods, or photographing in restricted areas is allowed.

Can I sketch inside the galleries?

Feel free to bring pencil and paper to sketch within our permanent collection galleries. Pens, markers, water, charcoal, pastels, paints, and easels are not allowed in the galleries. Some special exhibitions may have different rules.

Do you accept art donations?

We do not accept unsolicited art donations.

Do you do appraisal/conservation of works of art?

Unfortunately, we do not offer appraisal or conservation services.

Do you have restrooms?

Yes, restrooms are located on every floor for museum visitors.

Is there a nursing room?

No, there is not a nursing room at Mint Museum Randolph.

Are food and drinks allowed?

Food and drink are not allowed in the galleries under any circumstances.

Is smoking allowed?

The Mint Museum is a smoke free institution.

Does the museum rent spaces?

Yes, Mint Museum Randolph and Uptown both rent spaces for personal and company functions. Please visit our Museum Rentals page to learn more or call at 704.337.2108.

[Rent the Museum](https://www.mintmuseum.org/rent/)

Do you have WiFi?

Yes, both museum locations have free WiFi. Ask guest services for the password.
